column1: The fact that people go to the Louvre museum in Paris to see the original painting Mona Lisa when they can see a reproduction anywhere leads us to question some assumptions about the role of museums of fine art in today’s world
column2: 人们在任何地方都能看到《蒙娜丽莎》的复制品，却仍然前往巴黎卢浮宫观看原作。这一事实促使我们重新审视有关美术馆在当今世界所起作用的一些既有看法。

column1: One of the most famous works of art in the world is Leonardo da Vinci’s Mona Lisa.
column2: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇的《蒙娜丽莎》是世界上最著名的艺术作品之一。
column3: One of the most famous|最著名的……之一
column4: works of art|n. 艺术作品

column1: Nearly everyone who goes to see the original will already be familiar with it from reproductions, but they accept that fine art is more rewardingly viewed in its original form.
column2: 前去看原画的人几乎都已通过复制品熟悉了这幅画，但他们认同，欣赏美术作品的原作更有收获。

column1: However, if Mona Lisa was a famous novel, few people would bother to go to a museum to read the writer’s actual manuscript rather than a printed reproduction.
column2: 然而，假如《蒙娜丽莎》是一部著名小说，很少有人会特意跑去博物馆读作家的手稿，而放着印刷本不读。

column1: This might be explained by the fact that the novel has evolved precisely because of technological developments that made it possible to print out huge numbers of texts, whereas oil paintings have always been produced as unique objects.
column2: 这或许可以用以下事实来解释。小说之所以发展起来，恰恰是因为技术进步使文本可以大量印刷，而每幅油画从来都是作为独一无二的作品创作出来的。

column1: In addition, it could be argued that the practice of interpreting or ‘reading’ each medium follows different conventions.
column2: 此外，还可以认为，人们诠释或「阅读」不同艺术媒介时，遵循的惯例也各不相同。

column1: With novels, the reader attends mainly to the meaning of words rather than the way they are printed on the page, whereas the ‘reader’ of a painting must attend just as closely to the material form of marks and shapes in the picture as to any ideas they may signify.
column2: 读小说时，读者主要关注的是词语的含义，而非它们印在书页上的样子；“读”画的人则必须同样仔细地关注两方面：一是画中笔触和形状的具体形态，二是它们可能表达的意思。

column1: Yet it has always been possible to make very accurate facsimiles of pretty well any fine art work.
column2: 不过，几乎任何美术作品历来都可以仿制得十分逼真。

column1: The seven surviving versions of Mona Lisa bear witness to the fact that in the 16th century, artists seemed perfectly content to assign the reproduction of their creations to their workshop apprentices as regular ‘bread and butter’ work.
column2: 现存的七个《蒙娜丽莎》版本证明，在16世纪，画家们似乎很乐意把复制自己作品的活儿交给工作室的学徒，当作他们日常谋生的工作。

column1: And today the task of reproducing pictures is incomparably more simple and reliable, with reprographic techniques that allow the production of high-quality prints made exactly to the original scale, with faithful colour values, and even with duplication of the surface relief of the painting.
column2: 如今，复制画作的工作简单、可靠得多。图像复制技术可以制作高质量的印刷品，尺寸与原作完全相同，色彩明暗忠实于原作，甚至连画面表层的凹凸纹理都能复现。

column1: But despite an implicit recognition that the spread of good reproductions can be culturally valuable, museums continue to promote the special status of original work.
column2: 不过，尽管美术馆也默认传播优质复制品可以有文化价值，它们仍然推崇原作的特殊地位。

column1: Unfortunately, this seems to place severe limitations on the kind of experience offered to visitors.
column2: 遗憾的是，这似乎大大限制了参观者所能获得的观展体验。
column5: place severe limitations on|对……加以严格限制

column1: One limitation is related to the way the museum presents its exhibits.
column2: 其中一项限制与美术馆展示展品的方式有关。

column1: As repositories of unique historical objects, art museums are often called ‘treasure houses’.
column2: 美术馆收藏着独一无二的历史物件，因此常被称为「宝库」。

column1: We are reminded of this even before we view a collection by the presence of security guards, attendants, ropes and display cases to keep us away from the exhibits.
column2: 我们甚至还没看见藏品，就已经受到这样的提醒：现场有保安、工作人员、隔离绳和展示柜，让我们与展品保持距离。
column3: are reminded of|被提醒而想到
column11: keep us away from|让我们与……保持距离

column1: In many cases, the architectural style of the building further reinforces that notion.
column2: 在许多情况下，美术馆建筑本身的风格还会进一步强化这种印象。
column3: In many cases|在许多情况下

column1: In addition, a major collection like that of London’s National Gallery is housed in numerous rooms, each with dozens of works, any one of which is likely to be worth more than all the average visitor possesses.
column2: 此外，像伦敦国家美术馆这样的大型馆藏，分布在许多展厅里，每个展厅都有数十件作品。随便哪一件的价值，都很可能超过普通参观者的全部家当。
column4: is housed in|收藏或陈列于
column8: any one of which|其中的任何一件
column10: be worth more than|比……更值钱

column1: In a society that judges the personal status of the individual so much by their material worth, it is therefore difficult not to be impressed by one’s own relative ‘worthlessness’ in such an environment.
column2: 如果一个社会如此看重个人的物质财富，以此评判一个人的社会地位，那么身处这样的环境，人就很难不深感自己相形之下如此「不值钱」。
column6: material worth|n. 所拥有的物质财富

column1: Furthermore, consideration of the ‘Value’ of the original work in its treasure house setting impresses upon the viewer that, since these works were originally produced, they have been assigned a huge monetary value by some person or institution more powerful than themselves.
column2: 再者，在这样的「宝库」中思量原作的「价值」，观者会清楚地意识到，自这些作品问世以来，已有比观者自己更有权势的个人或机构给它们定下了极高的金钱价值。

column1: Evidently, nothing the viewer thinks about the work is going to alter that value, and so today’s viewer is deterred from trying to extend that spontaneous, immediate, self-reliant kind of reading which would originally have met the work.
column2: 显然，观者对作品的任何看法都改变不了这个价值。因此，如今的观者很难再尝试像作品问世之初的人那样，把自发、直接、凭自身判断的解读继续深入下去。
column7: is deterred from|因受阻而却步
column14: met the work|面对这件作品

column1: The visitor may then be struck by the strangeness of seeing such diverse paintings, drawings and sculptures brought together in an environment for which they were not originally created.
column2: 随后，参观者可能会觉得奇怪：如此多样的绘画、素描和雕塑作品被放在一起，而艺术家最初创作这些作品时，并非要将它们置于这样的环境中。

column1: This ‘displacement effect’ is further heightened by the sheer volume of exhibits.
column2: 单是展品数量之多，就进一步加剧了这种「错置效应」。

column1: In the case of a major collection, there are probably more works on display than we could realistically view in weeks or even months.
column2: 就大型馆藏而言，展出的作品很可能多到我们即使花上数周甚至数月，实际上也看不完。

column1: This is particularly distressing because time seems to be a vital factor in the appreciation of all art forms.
column2: 这一点尤其令人苦恼，因为在欣赏各种艺术形式时，时间似乎都是至关重要的因素。

column1: A fundamental difference between paintings and other art forms is that there is no prescribed time over which a painting is viewed.
column2: 绘画与其他艺术形式的一个根本区别在于，观看一幅画要花多长时间，并无规定。

column1: By contrast, the audience encounters an opera or a play over a specific time, which is the duration of the performance.
column2: 相比之下，观众欣赏歌剧或戏剧要经历一段固定的时间，就是演出本身的时长。

column1: Similarly, novels and poems are read in a prescribed temporal sequence, whereas a picture has no clear place at which to start viewing or at which to finish.
column2: 同样，读小说和诗歌有既定的先后顺序，看一幅画却没有明确的起点或终点。
column6: temporal sequence|n. 时间上的先后顺序

column1: Thus art works themselves encourage us to view them superficially, without appreciating the richness of detail and labour that is involved.
column2: 因此，艺术品本身也使我们容易看得浮光掠影，体会不到作品中丰富的细节以及投入其中的心血。

column1: Consequently, the dominant critical approach becomes that of the art historian, a specialised academic approach devoted to ‘discovering the meaning’ of art within the cultural context of its time.
column2: 这样一来，占主导地位的艺术评论方式便成了艺术史学家的做法：采用专门的学术方法，在艺术作品所属时代的文化背景中「发掘其意义」。
column5: critical approach|n. 艺术评论方法
column12: of its time|属于其所处时代的

column1: This is in perfect harmony with the museum’s function, since the approach is dedicated to seeking out and conserving ‘authentic’, ‘original’ readings of the exhibits.
column2: 这与美术馆的职能完全一致，因为这种方法致力于探寻并保存对展品「真实的」「原初的」解读。
column3: in perfect harmony with|与……完全一致

column1: Again, this seems to put paid to that spontaneous, participatory criticism which can be found in abundance in criticism of classic works of literature, but is absent from most art history.
column2: 这似乎也让那种自发、参与式的评论无从开展。这样的评论在对经典文学作品的评论中随处可见，大多数艺术史论述中却看不到。
column9: classic works of literature|经典文学作品

column1: The displays of art museums serve as a warning of what critical practices can emerge when spontaneous criticism is suppressed.
column2: 美术馆的陈列方式给了我们一个警示：当自发的评论受到压制时，会出现怎样的艺术评论方式。

column1: The museum public, like any other audience, experience art more rewardingly when given the confidence to express their views.
column2: 和其他观众一样，当美术馆的参观者有信心表达自己的看法时，欣赏艺术也会更有收获。
column8: express their views|表达自己的看法

column1: If appropriate works of fine art could be rendered permanently accessible to the public by means of high-fidelity reproductions, as literature and music already are, the public may feel somewhat less in awe of them.
column2: 如果能通过高度逼真的复制品，让公众像接触文学和音乐一样，随时都能接触到适合这样呈现的美术作品，那么公众对这些作品的敬畏之心或许会稍减一些。

column1: Unfortunately, that may be too much to ask from those who seek to maintain and control the art establishment.
column2: 遗憾的是，对于那些想要维持并掌控美术界现有体制的人来说，这个要求也许过高了。
